reason: The passage depicts Yahweh actively intervening to deliver the Hebrew people of Samaria from siege and famine. Yahweh sends a prophecy through Elisha promising abundant food at the gate (predicting that flour and barley will be cheap and available), and then directly causes the Aramean army to flee by miraculously making them hear phantom sounds of approaching rescue forces. This divine intervention results in the city being relieved from starvation and siege, demonstrating that helping the Hebrew people is indeed one of Yahweh's operative goals in this passage.
